races.name: Worcester Racecourse Ladies Day 6th June Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Queensbury Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 88-day break returning from wind operation, higher rating but poor recent chase form
runners_data.comment: Good second at Windsor in January & has had wind op since below-par run on heavy at Kelso
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at Kelso in February last time to make it 0-4 over fences but that was on heavy going and he's had a wind op since, while the return to a right-handed track is a likely plus; good second at Windsor (3m, soft) in January and he seems fine on good ground; solid claims if back on song.

runners_data.name: Court In A Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer race-fit from 26 days ago, thrives on good ground with solid recent handicap form
runners_data.comment: In pretty good form over hurdles this spring and he may well improve for going chasing
runners_data.spotlight: All eight of his races have been on good ground; this bumper and two-time novice hurdle winner (including here) has been running pretty well in staying handicap hurdles this spring and he may well improve for going chasing, which was the case with his useful dam Aimigayle.

races.paceDynamic: Queensbury Boy and Court In A Storm are both hold-up horses, creating a tactical dilemma in this two-runner affair. With no natural pace-setter, one will need to go forward reluctantly or they'll crawl early and sprint late. The reluctant leader will likely get soft fractions and kick clear, while the trailer faces a tough task giving the leader too much rope over this stamina-sapping trip. This race shape strongly favours whichever horse can secure the lead and control the tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Queensbury Boy Leads
scenarios.trigger: If Queensbury Boy takes up the running from the start.
scenarios.body: James Bowen gets soft fractions on the front end and can kick clear when ready, making full use of his higher official rating. Court In A Storm faces an impossible task trying to reel him in from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Court In A Storm Forward
scenarios.trigger: If Court In A Storm goes forward early despite his hold-up style.
scenarios.body: The Kim Bailey runner gets first run and uses his better recent form to dominate, while Queensbury Boy's 88-day absence and poor recent record over fences tells. Court In A Storm's superior fitness edge proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crawling Pace Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If both horses refuse to go forward early and crawl for two miles.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where Court In A Storm's recent race fitness and Tom Bellamy's tactical awareness prove crucial in a driving finish. Queensbury Boy's long layoff undermines his finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Blunders Decide
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors early in the race separate the pair significantly.
scenarios.body: The better jumper gains an unassailable advantage that proves impossible to peg back over the remaining distance. Technical proficiency at the obstacles becomes the determining factor rather than pure ability.

watchPoints.text: Both horses are hold-up types so watch the early pace - whichever goes forward first gains a huge tactical advantage
Queensbury Boy has been 0-4 over fences and the long break plus wind surgery adds uncertainty to his chances
Court In A Storm has won twice over hurdles at this track and handles the good ground perfectly

races.name: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guarenteed Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Quick Sharpener
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to Jamie Snowden after struggling for previous connections, with 108 days off and the headgear retained suggesting they're taking time to get him right
runners_data.comment: Struggled on final three runs but handy mark if change of stables has prompted a revival
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled last season on final three runs for the Newland/Insole yard; however, he won off 4lb higher at Bangor (2m4f, good) last April so has a handy mark to work with if a change of scenery has prompted a revival; new yard is enjoying a good month; remains in the same ownership.

runners_data.name: Delpotro
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner for in-form Charlie Longsdon yard, proven winner at similar distances on good ground with tactical advantage of dictating pace in small field
runners_data.comment: Returned from break to finish 3rd at Plumpton; this front-runner could be tough to reel in
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; won twice at Sedgefield last year (good to firm/good; up to extended 2m3f) and returned from a break to finish third of five at Plumpton (2m1f, good to soft) in March, not beaten far; could be tough to reel in.

runners_data.name: Beep Beep Becky
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making handicap debut off low mark, but poor hurdles form suggests she may struggle to bridge the class gap despite receiving significant weight
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced point runner-up who could improve for going chasing; watch the betting
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten on all four hurdle starts, most recently when 9-1 for her handicap debut at Catterick (3m1f, good) in March; however, this lightly raced point runner-up could be suited by the switch to fences and drop back in trip; a tongue-tie goes on; a market move would be interesting.

races.paceDynamic: Delpotro will lead unchallenged from the front in this three-runner affair, setting his own tempo without any early pressure. Quick Sharpener will sit prominently in second, while Beep Beep Becky drops out the back as the hold-up runner. With no pace pressure on Delpotro and plenty of time to organize over 2m5f, he can dictate fractions that suit his front-running style perfectly. This race shape strongly favors the leader and prominent runners, as the lack of early pace will make it difficult for the hold-up runner to close from too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Delpotro Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Delpotro jumps cleanly and maintains his rhythm throughout
scenarios.body: He can kick clear turning for home without having been pressured early, using his superior tactical position to full advantage. Sean Bowen can time his move perfectly from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Quick Sharpener Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Delpotro makes jumping errors or tires in the straight
scenarios.body: Gavin Sheehan can track the leader closely and strike when Delpotro falters, benefiting from his prominent position. His higher official rating suggests he has more ability on his day.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Blowout
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling slow even for a small field
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where class could tell and positioning becomes crucial. Quick Sharpener's higher rating could prove decisive in such circumstances.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Beep Becky Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders compound badly or fall late in the race
scenarios.body: The mare could benefit from clear jumping and inherit the race from behind. Her point-to-point background suggests she can stay this trip strongly.

watchPoints.text: Watch Delpotro's jumping rhythm early - any mistakes will compromise his front-running tactics and hand initiative to Quick Sharpener
Monitor Quick Sharpener's position tracking Delpotro - if he gets too keen or too far back, his prominent style won't be effective in this small field
Observe Beep Beep Becky's jumping fluency as any errors will make her task from the back even more difficult
Check the early pace setting by Delpotro - if he goes too fast early, it could set up a collapse scenario for the closers
Watch for any market moves on Quick Sharpener given the stable change and long absence

races.name: Ludford Car Parts Group Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hidden Fortune
runners_data.note: Front-running style with class advantage but 36 days off and needs to prove stamina over this extended trip

runners_data.name: Mrs Cravatte
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from poor trainer form but her stalking style could benefit from the certain strong pace ahead
runners_data.comment: Unable to get competitive in points and soundly beaten in a bumper and a maiden hurdle
runners_data.spotlight: Unable to get competitive in points and soundly beaten in a bumper and a maiden hurdle; others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Lady Kara
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with solid recent form but 0-8 record suggests vulnerability when pace gets serious
runners_data.comment: 0-8 but she's been in good form this spring and there's every chance she'll be bang there
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8, with five of those defeats over hurdles, and it's possible she's vulnerable to stronger stayers at this trip; however, she's run well on both starts this spring and there's every chance that she'll be bang there.

runners_data.name: Kittys Glance
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from wind surgery with hood retained, 55 days off but style suits race shape perfectly
runners_data.comment: Won at Huntingdon in March and pedigree provides optimism that she will keep progressing
runners_data.spotlight: Following wind surgery she settled better in a first-time hood (retained) to win at Huntingdon in March on her second hurdle start (2m3f, good; bled from the nose); carries a penalty today but her pedigree provides optimism that she will continue to progress.

runners_data.name: Liasse d'Argent
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 5lb claiming jockey, limited ability shown but running style matches likely race development
runners_data.comment: Showed some ability at Stratford last month but not enough to suggest she'll threaten here
runners_data.spotlight: Showed some ability when sixth at 200-1 at Stratford (2m, good) on her second start, but not enough to suggest she'll pose a threat today.

runners_data.name: Nannymooresbridge
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning after 194 days and wind surgery, poor recent form but could force stronger early pace
runners_data.comment: Tailed off in both bumpers and pulled up at 300-1 on hurdle debut last October
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off in both bumpers and pulled up at 300-1 on hurdle debut last October; a transformation is needed following wind surgery.

races.paceDynamic: Hidden Fortune, Lady Kara, and Nannymooresbridge will ensure a strong early gallop from the start, with all three confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the lead. This sustained pace will stretch the field over 2m3½f and test stamina reserves in the final half-mile. The relentless gallop will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses Kittys Glance and Liasse d'Argent to come from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours closers and hold-up performers who can benefit from the certain strong pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain a genuine strong pace throughout
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will deplete the leaders' stamina reserves and create perfect conditions for a closer to strike late. Kittys Glance's proven ability to settle and finish strongly makes her ideally suited to this unfolding.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders can dictate more sensible fractions early
scenarios.body: A more measured pace would allow the front-runner to retain enough stamina to resist late challengers. Hidden Fortune's class edge and recent form gives her the best chance of controlling the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Times Move
scenarios.trigger: If Mrs Cravatte can track the leaders without getting involved in early pace battles
scenarios.body: She could benefit from a perfect stalking position behind the battling front-runners before making her move. Her prominent style positions her ideally between the pace and the closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Nannymooresbridge's return from wind surgery sees dramatic improvement
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly competitive Nannymooresbridge could force even stronger early fractions than anticipated. This would maximize the advantage for any horse able to settle and produce a sustained late run.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Nannymooresbridge shows early pace improvement as this could create an unsustainably fast gallop that destroys all front-runners
Monitor how aggressively Hidden Fortune and Lady Kara engage early as both need to prove stamina over this trip
Observe if Kittys Glance settles cleanly in her hood as her hold-up style is perfectly suited to exploit the expected pace
Check whether the three confirmed front-runners actually engage in serious pace battles or if one tries to dictate more sensible fractions
Watch for Mrs Cravatte's positioning early as she needs to avoid getting dragged into pace battles to maximize her stalking advantage

races.name: CopyBet Says Thank You To Hereford Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Catwalk Girl
runners_data.note: Front-runner fresh off a 5-day turnaround from her Huntingdon win with confident booking of conditional jockey retaining the ride
runners_data.comment: Won off this mark on chase debut at Huntingdon last week; promise over hurdles previously
runners_data.spotlight: Fell on handicap hurdle debut at Ludlow last month and this point winner scored at Huntingdon (2m7f, good) last Thursday on her first chase start; she capitalised on the early fall of the favourite last time, and she needs to transfer her form back to hurdles, but she has shown promise in this sphere and races off the same mark as last week; wears first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Border Gem
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with useful course form but concerning 0-10 record despite multiple placed efforts
runners_data.comment: Rallied at Taunton on first crack at 3m and today's extra yardage could be in her favour
runners_data.spotlight: 0-10 but she ran well when second here (2m3f, good) in March and rallied for a respectable fifth at Taunton (good) three weeks ago on her first crack at 3m; shaped last time as though today's extra yardage could be in her favour and she might be in the mix.

runners_data.name: Campaign Trail
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with class edge and top weight penalty, returning from 41-day break for powerful Kim Bailey stable
runners_data.comment: Ran well when third at Southwell (3m, good) last time and he's entitled to respect
runners_data.spotlight: He's returned from a break in good heart this year, finishing fourth at Market Rasen (2m7f, soft) before getting closer to the target when 3l third at Southwell (3m, good); entitled to respect.

runners_data.name: Heard That
runners_data.note: Hold-up type better over fences than hurdles with unpredictable form patterns and fresh off 19-day rest
runners_data.comment: Better chaser than hurdler and not easy to predict in either discipline; tries blinkers
runners_data.spotlight: Better chaser than hurdler and not easy to predict in either discipline; finished runner-up over C&D in March but then tailed off at Perth, again over hurdles; blinkers go on.

runners_data.name: I Am Spider Man
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse showing signs of return to form for new connections after 6-day quick turnaround
runners_data.comment: Returned to form when going close at Newton Abbot & he's a major player if backing that up
runners_data.spotlight: 9yo who hasn't won since July 2024 but he returned to form when going close at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) last Wednesday on his second start for this yard; major player if backing up that latest performance.

races.paceDynamic: Catwalk Girl will dictate from the front as the sole confirmed leader, with Campaign Trail likely tracking in second through the early stages. The lack of other pace pressers means Catwalk Girl can control fractions without being harassed, creating a sustainable rhythm over this stamina-sapping 3m1½f trip. The hold-up quartet of Border Gem, Heard That, and I Am Spider Man will need the pace to collapse late, but with only one horse setting the tempo, this sets up ideally for prominent racers and those who can travel kindly in behind the leaders rather than needing a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Catwalk Girl maintains her jumping and isn't pressured early
scenarios.body: Her recent Huntingdon win shows she's in form and can dictate at her own pace, while Campaign Trail can track and pounce if the leader weakens. The lack of pace pressure plays directly into the hands of these two forward-running types.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Staying Power
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes pedestrian and it becomes a stamina test
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their chance in a slowly-run affair where the 3m1½f distance becomes the key factor rather than tactical positioning. I Am Spider Man's recent Newton Abbot near-miss suggests he's finding form at the right time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Move Success
scenarios.trigger: If Campaign Trail or another prominent runner applies pressure from halfway
scenarios.body: This creates a more genuine pace that could find out Catwalk Girl's stamina while still not being fast enough early to set up the hold-up horses. Campaign Trail's class edge from the Kim Bailey yard could prove decisive in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Catwalk Girl goes too fast early trying to assert dominance
scenarios.body: The leader empties out in the straight after dictating too aggressively, leaving it to the closers to pick up the pieces. Border Gem's course form gives her an edge if it becomes a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Catwalk Girl's jumping under pressure - any early mistakes could disrupt her rhythm and change the entire race dynamic
Campaign Trail's fitness after 41 days off - needs to be sharp enough to take advantage of his prominent position
I Am Spider Man's stamina reserves at 9 years old over this extended trip on quick turnaround
Border Gem's ability to overcome her poor strike rate despite consistently hitting the frame
The pace through the middle section - if it becomes truly pedestrian it transforms the finish completely

races.name: First Past The Post At CopyBet Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Man Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner who needs to prove fitness after 166-day absence but has solid form when right
runners_data.comment: In good form before Christmas; should be sharper for a recent Flat fifth; considered
runners_data.spotlight: In good form without winning (runner-up over 2m3f at Taunton) before Christmas and should be sharper for a recent fifth on the Flat at Bath; this veteran needs considering.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with good trainer strike-rate, suited by steady pace he can control
runners_data.comment: Not disgraced when third of five in 2m2f Fontwell h'cap last month; needs to build on it
runners_data.spotlight: Largely below par since scoring at Huntingdon (2m4f) last May but he wasn't disgraced when third of five in 2m2f Fontwell handicap last month; needs to build on it now.

runners_data.name: Jackeline
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who was course winner but looked poor last time, needs significant bounce back
runners_data.comment: Course winner in 2024; last of seven at Newton Abbot last month; others   much preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner in 2024 but she failed to take to fences last season and came in last of seven back in this sphere at Newton Abbot (2m) last month; others are much preferred.

runners_data.name: Jack Hoola
runners_data.note: Talented hold-up horse returning from 74-day break, twice winner but needs to prove current form
runners_data.comment: Off since below-par Doncaster seventh in January; needs to bounce back after a layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Scored twice (around 2m4f) at Huntingdon and Southwell late in 2025 but off since a below-par seventh at Doncaster (2m3f) in January when also not looking the easiest of rides; needs to bounce back after a layoff.

runners_data.name: Midnight Pass
runners_data.note: Low-mileage 5yo hold-up type on good handicap mark, solid return run suggests more to come
runners_data.comment: Solid fourth on h'cap debut at Taunton 20 days ago; she can do better off a 2lb lower mark
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo who returned from six months off with a solid fourth of nine on her handicap debut at Taunton (2m3f) 20 days ago; she can do better off a 2lb lower mark.

runners_data.name: Ice Jet
runners_data.note: Progressive 4yo hold-up runner from top yard, wind surgery clearly helped based on improved recent second
runners_data.comment: Much improved on back of a wind op when second at Wetherby latest; up 6lb but major shout
runners_data.spotlight: A fair ex-Irish Flat maiden; brought along steadily over hurdles for current yard before much improved on his handicap debut (on the back of a wind op) when second of 11 at Wetherby (2m) in March, only just failing after a late blunder; major shout despite a 6lb rise.

runners_data.name: The Padster
runners_data.note: Limited hold-up horse with breathing issues, hard to fancy despite cheekpieces addition
runners_data.comment: Had breathing surgery before remote Exeter fourth 25 days ago; cheekpieces are now tried
runners_data.spotlight: Only modest form shown thus far and he had breathing surgery before coming in a remote fourth of nine in 2m1f Exeter handicap 25 days ago; cheekpieces are now tried.

runners_data.name: Launceston
runners_data.note: Weak maiden struggling over hurdles, hard to see turning form around off long absence
runners_data.comment: Yet to show much for current yard over hurdles and last of nine on Flat in February
runners_data.spotlight: Modest Flat maiden for Sir Mark Prescott; yet to show much for his current yard over hurdles and last of nine back on the Flat at Wolverhampton in February; hard to warm to.

runners_data.name: Celine Man
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse with poor recent form and tendency to fade, easy to dismiss
runners_data.comment: Offered little in a pair of 2m Huntingdon handicaps for current yard in February
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly-raced 8yo who offered little in a pair of 2m Huntingdon handicaps for his current yard in February; easy to look elsewhere.

races.paceDynamic: Man Of The Sea and Ikigai Star will likely dispute the early lead, with both comfortable prominent runners who won't set a punishing gallop over this trip. The majority of the field are hold-up horses (Jackeline, Jack Hoola, Midnight Pass, Ice Jet, The Padster, Celine Man) meaning the pace could become quite steady through the middle stages. With limited early pace and a bunched field likely turning for home, this race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close to the pace and have something left to kick when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Man Of The Sea and Ikigai Star control the tempo without excessive pressure
scenarios.body: The steady pace suits their stamina profiles and they can resist the late challenges from a bunched pack behind. Hold-up horses struggle to make up significant ground in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Late Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes very sedate and the field remains tightly bunched turning in
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the best handicapped and freshest horses can unleash telling kicks. Jack Hoola and Ice Jet benefit from racing off lower weights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners go too fast early trying to shake off the pack
scenarios.body: Man Of The Sea and Ikigai Star empty out in the final furlong after setting unsustainable fractions. The hold-up horses sweep past tired leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If one of the outsiders finds significant improvement or the favourites underperform
scenarios.body: The Padster benefits from his recent breathing surgery and cheekpieces addition, or Midnight Pass shows natural progression as a low-mileage 5yo. The race falls apart for the market leaders.

watchPoints.text: Man Of The Sea jumps poorly early or shows signs of rustiness after his 166-day layoff
Ice Jet gets too far back in running as many hold-up horses could get caught behind a wall of horses
Ikigai Star and Man Of The Sea go faster than intended if they clash for the early lead
Jack Hoola shows any signs of needing the run after his 74-day absence from racing
The Padster jumps any better with the cheekpieces fitted for the first time

races.name: Hereford Season Finale Open National Hunt Flat Race (Cat 1 Elimination) (GBB)

runners_data.name: Five Lanes
runners_data.comment: Ran out on last month's debut in British maiden point; may be best watched on bumper debut
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to three winners; ran out on last month's debut in a British maiden point (2m4f, good to soft); may be best watched on bumper debut.

runners_data.name: Master Roque
runners_data.comment: Mid-division on debut in valuable bumper at Newbury; could have a big part to play
runners_data.spotlight: £54,000 3yo who contested a valuable bumper at Newbury (2m, good to soft) on his debut last month, finishing 13th of 20 at 22-1 against several previous winners; that gives him something to build on and he could have a big part to play.

runners_data.name: Lost In The Dream
runners_data.comment: Defied evident inexperience to win on debut at Taunton and could have plenty more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Bred to be talented and he defied his evident inexperience to win at 7-2 on last month's debut at Taunton (2m, good), the first two clear; he could have plenty more to offer and holds strong claims under a penalty.

runners_data.name: Mayo
runners_data.comment: Showed ability on the first of his two starts but improvement necessary on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed ability when 11l fourth of six on debut at Stratford (2m, good to firm) last August, then took a backwards step at Worcester (2m, good) in September; has since left Christian Williams and improvement is needed on this first outing for Mickey Bowen; remains in same ownership.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Fernand
runners_data.comment: Down the field on both starts (2m, soft), most recently when 150-1 at Stratford in March
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field on both starts (2m, soft), most recently when 150-1 at Stratford in March; others are preferred.
